utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. While we are waiting for him, could I briefly deal with the following matter: The Prosecution requested - and I'm talking about Exhibit D471 - that the Defence provide them with information concerning the provenance of that document which was MFI'd. The Chamber would like to know whether the Prosecution has received the necessary information, and if so, whether in light of that information it has any objections to the admission of D471.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No, we have not. But I'll address that with Mr. Lukic during the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzida.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Stojanovic will now continue his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, following up on yesterday's questioning of the witness, I propose that after you decided to admit his statement that you also admit document 65 ter 09142 as an attachment to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber. One second, please. The Chamber just will verify what exactly it is. It is an associated exhibit and it is -- let me have a look. It's the document of the 4th Corps Command, strictly confidential. Yes, no objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 9142 receives number D491, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D491 is admitted. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read a brief summary of the evidence of Witness Milorad Dzida, and I will ask him a few short questions later. Witness Milorad Dzida was a company commander in the 215th Mountain Brigade of the 4th Corps of the JNA at the outbreak of the war. From the 9th of August, 1993, after he had been wounded several times, he was reassigned to the 7th Battalion of the 1st Romanija Brigade to the duty of the deputy commander for intelligence at which position he remained until the 17th of October, 1994. He then took over the duty of the battalion commander at Nisici where he remained until the end of the war. The witness talks about the duties which he received from the command of the 7th Battalion on the 6th of February, 1994, after the incident at the Markale market. He says that, as an intelligence officer, he took a team comprising the representatives of the Main Staff of the VRS, the SRK, the UNPROFOR, and his brigade to the firing position of the 120-millimetre mortar. He had the occasion to hear the words of the interpreter, who was a member of the UNPROFOR team, that it was not possible that on the previous day it was fired from these weapons. Warrant Officer Jakovljevic, who was a member of the team, drew up reports about this incident for the needs of the SRK on behalf of the brigade. Witness Dzida further testifies that several days later, a group of UNPROFOR officers carried out inspection once again together with a female interpreter. When the officers inquired, she interpreted the words of the French major who said that the 7th Battalion had nothing to do with the incident at Markale. Further, the witness points out that they had strict orders to observe any cease-fire or truce and that the fire of his battalion was always aimed at firing positions of the enemy and never at civilians or civilian facilities. The civilians in the city could only be hit if military targets were targeted and if such targets were located close to civilian facilities. He also testifies about the way that the opposing side waged war, pointing out that the forces of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were far superior with regards to manpower, mentioning as an example that facing his battalion was the 110th Brigade of the 1st Corps of the Army of the BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statement, which you accepted as true and correct yesterday and today, you talk about having had the occasion to learn about the fact that members of paramilitary formations, who were ethnic Muslims, were being armed. Could you tell me, where did you receive such information and were you personally familiar with such events?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a couple of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you don't mind, since there is two bases of knowledge in that question, if he could please separate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please split up your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The first question which I would like to ask you is whether you had personal and direct information about these events.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had personal and direct information about these events in the building where I lived. In December, bars were placed in the common basements in the building and the residents could no longer enter this area. You had to address two people if you wanted to take what -- the food that you had prepared for the winter. So on the 6th of January I could see for myself because I had a conflict with the president of the residents union.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please slow down when you speak because your speed of speech is such that the interpreters cannot follow you. You said you had a conflict with the president of the residents union. Please proceed and finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the tenants council, yes. Because I -- I could not leave in the basement my winter preserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what you found in the basement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they placed weapons there during the night and there were bars on the door so nobody could enter. When I went to the police station to report this, we never received any response from them. After me, a neighbour also reported this, and five or six days later we had still not received any answer. I know, I heard from Radomir Neskovic who was detained there, he had remained in my apartment, I heard from him that weapons were being kept down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that this all happened in December. December of what year, Mr. Dzida?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] December 1991, late December 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Court if you learned indirectly anything about where the paramilitary formations that you talked about, the Patriotic League and the Green Berets, were being trained for the forthcoming war events?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the training was conducted in an area in Trebevic. The place is called Dobro Vode, and then the Unica hotel at Igman, also the Mraziste and Igman hotels. My colleague, Mustafa Gegaj, spent quite a long time at training in Igman, and during the war he worked as deputy commander in charge of intelligence in the Hrasnica Brigade. There were several colleagues who spent 15 to 20 days at the training sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where do you have this information from?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned this because Mustafa was absent from work for two and a half months, and then later, there was also a man who used to work in the MUP and remained in Hrasnica. He published a book and the book includes Gegaj's picture. It's called "Hrasnicka Golgota" or "The Hrasnica Passion."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you about the period in 1994 when you performed the duty as the deputy commander of the 7th Battalion for intelligence. As a unit, was your zone of defence attacked by the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions. I remember the two most tragic attacks that they launched. One was on the 27th of May, 1994. That was when six of our men got killed at Zecija Glava and we had seven or eight wounded. Of the six men, four had been hit in the eye, in the head, that is to say. I even remember some of their names, if you would like to hear that. The other attack that they launched took place on the 18th of September, 1994. They then launched an attack along the entire line and the thrust was against two companies, the 4th and the 1st Companies, that is. And in both companies, around seven men got killed. And we also had some losses at Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned the Spicaste Stijene location. While you were performing the duty in the 7th Battalion, were any other attacks launched at the Spicaste Stijene positions by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most attacks were directed at the Spicaste Stijene location. There is a cave there and across from the cave and -- there is also a wooded area, so these parts are somewhat forward and they were the targets of attack. We couldn't carry out reconnaissance properly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Maybe I'm missing it, but if Mr. Stojanovic could assist me where he discusses Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the statement, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. If I'm missing -- if I'm missing it, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, Spicaste Stijene, where does it appear in the statement? Or in the 65 ter summary, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's paragraph 24 of his statement, only now it's been expanded in this answer. It's been expanded with this place name, but he does discuss the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean that the casualties described in May 1994, that is the events, and it very much looks like it, on the 27th of May, and that apart from that, locations mentioned which are not far away from Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. The link is clear now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. I will finish by this. Let me just ask one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As for the place names that you talked, Zecija Glava, Faletici, where was the area that you called Spicaste Stijene located?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across from Vasin Han, it's 8 to 9 kilometres from Spicaste Stijene across the defence area covered by my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was your battalion specifically in charge of the Spicaste Stijene area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers, Mr. Dzida. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Before we give an opportunity to start the cross-examination of the witness. Mr. Dzida, could you tell us how often approximately, as far as you know, did the ABiH forces try to take control over Spicaste Stijene? So I'm not talking about exchange of fire but I'm talking about an attempt to take control.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood. They tried to do that on several occasions. They even managed twice to take away parts of Spicaste Stijene from us and then we managed to recapture them. Later on we placed a wire fence that could stop their rockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm mainly interested in how many times. You said they succeeded twice and you then regained it. Apart from these successful attempts, how many attempts were there which then likely were unsuccessful? Was it three, was it ten, was it 20?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were many a number, but I can't remember the exact number. Quite a few attacks against Spicaste Stijene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some people would consider 20 quite a number, others would consider five quite a number, others would consider -- could you approximate, even if you don't know the exact number? Was it closer to five than it was to ten or closer to twenty or -- if you remember. If you say: I can't answer the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whenever they attempted to launch an attack against the zone of responsibility of the 7th Battalion, it was always via Spicaste Stijene. At least 15 times, if not more. But I'm certain it wasn't fewer than that. And these were quite violent attacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You find Mr. Weber to your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzida.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of your statement you indicate that you were wounded on two occasions. With respect to your first wounding, on the 4th of May, 1992, how long were you away from your duties with this injury?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, what -- do you have anything in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is all typed and signed. Typed text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you are -- Mr. Weber, I can imagine that if you refer to a certain paragraph of the statement, then the witness may want to read the statement because you refer to it. But would you -- is that your statement, Mr. Dzida, which you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, any notes on it or is it just the typewritten text?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are some minor corrections where there were typos, but I won't be using it because I'm quite familiar with what it contains more or less. On the 3rd of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Please put them away and don't consult them unless you have asked permission for that. Mr. Weber, whenever you refer to a paragraph, make sure that the witness understands exactly what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course. And, Your Honours, I'm mainly referring to the paragraph for the record's sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can ask the question without the reference to the paragraph, just because it's pretty simple information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could first put your question and then say for the Court the paragraphs also.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you about your first wounding on the 4th of May, 1992. How long were you away from your duties with this injury?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 3rd of May, 1994, my unit received a task to go to the Jewish cemetery sector in order to secure the withdrawal from the Marshal Tito barracks. It was the 4th Corps of the JNA --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir -- sorry to cut you off, sir, but if you could please listen to my question. It appears in your statement that you were injured on the 4th of May, 1992. I'm just simply asking you how long you were out with that injury. We can see the information that you're providing is part of your statement already. There is no need to repeat that. If you could just tell me how long were you out with that injury.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded on the 4th of May, 1992. I returned to the unit on crutches after the medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 4th of May in 1992 at quarter to 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now just to be sure: You were wounded on that day and you returned on that same day, with crutches, to your unit? Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the same day, after four or five hours of receiving treatment at the hospital, I returned to my unit because I knew -- I had a doctor in my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to be as efficient as possible, and we are under time restraints, Mr. Dzida. The shortest and accurate answer would have been: I was away only for a couple of hours. That's what Mr. Weber wanted to know, how long were you away. And whether there were a doctor or no doctor or whether it was on crutches or not, a couple of hours is apparently your answer to the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. But I'm a soldier, not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just listen to the questions carefully and try to answer them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you able to immediately return to active duty?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately. I returned to duty immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your statement you also discuss a second occasion where you were wounded on the 6th of May, 1993. Where were you when you sustained these injuries?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the defence sector at Vihari, Vihari Kijet [phoen], near Podgreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You indicate on the second occasion that you received a total of 21 wounds. How long were you away from active duty on the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, today I'm going to start by discussing the activities of the 216th JNA Brigade before it was renamed the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade. I'd just like to clarify initially a few things with you. Is it correct that you were first mobilised into the 216th Brigade between 30 June 1991 and 16 August 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation started on the 30th of June, 1991, and on the 16th of August, 1992, we returned the equipment. So that was the first mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. Then you were mobilised on a second occasion on 17 September 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, the 17th of September, 1991, the second mobilisation was carried out; that is to say, the additional mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D491 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it, Mr. Weber, I've got no idea where Vihari Kijet may be. If you could either clarify together with the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so that the answer serves its purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 4th Corps analysis dated 21 August 1991 that you discuss in a paragraph of your statement. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you also commented upon this document in your statement for the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I please have page 4 in both versions. And for the witness, I'm going to be focusing on information that's at the very top of the original. And for Your Honours, it's information in the centre of the page in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in your Mladic statement in paragraph 12, you discuss this report and it's similar to your discussion in the Karadzic statement. However, I'm going to read you an additional sentence which appeared in your Karadzic statement. I'm just simply asking you if you could confirm this. In your Karadzic statement, you added with respect to this document: "Response was very poor, which is confirmed in the above-mentioned document on page 4. The first paragraph that was shown to me which says that 1.218 soldiers did not respond to mobilisation. They were Muslim reservists."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to paragraph 12 in the Mladic statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is -- I'm referring to the -- my apologies for the confusion, thank you. I'm referring to paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I confused it with the Karadzic paragraph number. My apologies for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph 10 of?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Mladic statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you pointed at the differences with the Karadzic statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct. I apologise for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you need me to repeat your statement from the Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm still lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm still lost. I don't see the words "the response was poor" in paragraph 10. I see it in paragraph 12 and that's where it ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct. Sorry for the confusion. In the Mladic statement, he comments on the document on one occasion in paragraph 10. In the Karadzic statement, he commented on the document in two separate paragraphs. The now paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement had an additional comment that -- in the Karadzic statement that also made reference to this document which is now visible in the current paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement. I apologise for that confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: However, all what you have read out I don't see in paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct. I -- it was my confusion. Paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement -- all right. Let's just go through it. In paragraph 10 of the Mladic statement, there is reference to this document. In paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This is 0914 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct. In paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement, he discusses how the response was poor. Formerly in the Karadzic statement, that -- the paragraph that is now paragraph 12 of the Mladic statement made a second reference to the same document which is why I'm trying to get the witness to confirm now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to this document in the Karadzic case, you stated: "Response was very poor, which is confirmed in the above-mentioned document on page 4. The first paragraph that was shown to me which says that 1.218 soldiers did not respond to mobilisation. They were Muslim reservists." Do you stand by this statement on this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This goes for the entire brigade. This number of people did not respond, that's certain. These officers, NCOs, military conscripts, motor vehicles, and cattle. I don't see the number of people who did respond. I don't see that here at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So, sir, you confirm your previous statement that the -- in this document, the 1.218 soldiers that did not respond were Muslim reservists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not confirm that they were reservists. Most of those who did not respond were Muslims, because some Muslims did respond to the call up for our unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, the question to you was: Are the 1.218, all of them, are they all Muslims? That's the question. Not whether other Muslims did respond.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, approximately that would be the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's the ethnicity that we are asking for. The number is 1.218. Were they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time when we compiled that report, we didn't say whether it was just Muslims or whether there were some Serbs among them. At any rate, that's the number of people who did not respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the question now to you is whether those 1.218 were Muslims? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've told you that most of them were Muslims. As far as I can remember my previous answer to President Karadzic, it was the same, the same answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And "most of them," that means 95, 98 per cent of the number mentioned here? Close to that? Almost --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately that much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So almost all of them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30704.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, coming up before you will be a document dated 5 January 1995. It is a recommendation for decoration of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade from SRK commander Dragomir Milosevic. In this recommendation, General Milosevic discusses the experiences of the brigade from the 30th of June 1991 onward. I'm going to go through it with you part by part here. And if, sir, you could please listen to my questions, I'm just going to go step by step. In the first few sentences, he refers to operations in the Banja Luka sector between 1 July and 15 August 1991 which successfully secured the Mahovljani airport. Did you participate in these operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I participated but it wasn't an operation. We came there for training and by the way we also secured the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the middle of the first paragraph, General Milosevic discusses a series of tasks that were completed by the brigade between August 1991 and March 1992. He states: "In addition to its engagement in combat operations, the brigade also organised training of Serbs in crucial specialist areas ..." And he names some of these areas. Starting with the first one, is it correct that members of the 216th Brigade received specialist training in areas such as sniping?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you say that because you did not receive that training?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit -- as far as my unit is concerned, I don't think that anybody underwent such training.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you cannot exclude the possibility that others in the brigade received such training?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that others didn't go either. That's for sure. Because according to establishment, in a platoon there are three snipers, and these are ordinary M-76 snipers with ordinary optical sights. So according to establishment, these snipers did exist but nobody went for this kind of training, and I claim that with full responsibility. And also I'm going to ask you to make the Serbian letters more visible because I don't have the right glasses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If portions of anything should be enlarged, please ask for it. If there is a specific portion you can't read, although the text, of course, can be read to you as well. And do I understand that you are telling us that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right, if you were to enlarge it when you're putting a question to me, I mean the Serbian part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not used to being interrupted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document which is authored by Dragomir Milosevic, Major-General Dragomir Milosevic, says that organised training of Serbs in crucial specialist areas was performed. Do I understand that you say that this is a false report by Dragomir Milosevic? Because you deny that it's true, what is written in this report. So you say it's a false report or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I said. But units that responded to call-up had training every day. And it was tactical training and combat rules and so on, so I mean this is training, practical training, in the JNA. When people are called up, they should do something so they wouldn't just be sitting around. As for this kind of specific thing, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The report says that there was specialist training within this brigade for snipers. You're saying this didn't happen. Therefore, either the report is not true or what you're telling is not true. I'm not saying that you're intentionally saying something which is not true, but I'm saying the two contradict each other clearly. Any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just telling the truth and I am saying the truth, and I'm telling you that there were no sniper shooters. And when proposals are made, they are always exaggerated so that they would fair better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is about training of snipers, specialist training of snipers within the brigade. That's what the report is about. You say it's not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My unit did not give anyone, did not go out for training, and as far as I can remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about unit. I'm talking about specialist snipers training within the brigade as described in the report. If you say it's not true, then the document is inaccurate. If you say "I don't know" or "I wasn't aware of it," that's a different matter. I'm just trying to find out where we are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, there was no training, specialist training for snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no knowledge of such training. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The second area indicates that there was squad commander training. Did you receive this training as a company commander in the 216th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I underwent all training in peacetime before mobilisation; that is to say, starting with reserve officers school to - what was the name? - the training for platoon commanders, company commanders, and training for deputy commanders of battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You've mentioned that there was some training after you joined the 216th Brigade. What type of training was that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regular training that was planned. I joined the 16th in 75. The 216th Mountain Brigade, according to the war deployment of the then state, the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "regular training," what type of training are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every few years they asked us to come for some kind of training. After finishing reserve officers school, then I worked as a trainee. And then every two years there was training, and that was the plan of the JNA in the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could direct your attention back to the document in front of you, and if you have any trouble seeing it, please let us know. General Milosevic goes on to discuss some of the brigade's early operations between September 1991 and March 1992. He makes references to operations in Dubrovnik during this time. My question is very simple: Did you participate in these operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It indicates that another part of the brigade went to Borovo Naselje near Vukovar in Slavonia. Did you participate in these operations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Between which months did you go to Borovo Naselje? Specifically, was it with the rest of the brigade in November 1991 or that -- part of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of November 1991, when the fourteenth cease-fire was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you operated -- the part of your brigade that went, that you operated as a subordinate unit of Operation Group South?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we scroll down this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Borovo Naselje is continuing on the second page. That's also where Dubrovnik is found, Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where we couldn't see it earlier. So we now have it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, when you went to the area of Borovo Naselje in 1991, did your part of your brigade operate as part of Operation Group South, OG South?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they belonged to the Novi Sad Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would that be OG North? Do you know? If you don't know, that's fine too.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the third paragraph, I believe on the page in front of you, which is now the first full paragraph at the top of the English translation, General Milosevic states: "Parts of the brigade that were not engaged in the fighting in Eastern Slavonia and Dubrovnik were engaged in securing materiel and technical equipment in the Han Pijesak sector and securing transport from Ustikolina to the Slavonia front." Is this correct that this was the -- what the remainder of the brigade did who did not go to either Dubrovnik or Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were providing security. I don't remember this because I wasn't there for Ustikolina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30704 into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30704 receives number P6543, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6543 is admitted into evidence. Could we have a close look at the transcript in this respect. Yes, there we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before the next break, I just want to see if we can get through one relatively brief topic. In the supplemental statement that has been admitted in this case, you indicate that you returned to Ilidza after 16 August 1991. Is it correct that you then left Ilidza again in mid-September when you rejoined the 216th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to understand but the question was not put to me clearly. It is correct that I returned from Han Pijesak on the 16th of May, so then on the 17th of May -- or, rather, August, I -- I reported at the company. Then Hebib, the technical director, met me there --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could just cut you off before we get too far afield. Is it correct that you were in Ilidza between 16 August and 17 September 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am telling you that on the 17th, I think, August, I was at Ilidza. And -- I mean, later I was wasn't in Ilidza because I got this decision on annual leave, and I had an apartment at Dobrinja V, and they sent me off on holiday because they told me there was no work for me anymore. The technical director, Hebib Mustafa -- no, it wasn't Mustafa, but Hebib it was. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, did all this happen between the -- my questions are very simple: Did all this happen between the 17th of August and the 17th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you now that I was at Ilidza then and I did not go back to Ilidza until the additional mobilisation took place. I mean, there was no need for me to go there. I got this decision on annual leave and there was no need for me to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The remark you just made, I think, will be clear enough. In your previous testimony in the Karadzic case, this is at transcript page 29565, you stated: "In 1991 I left Ilidza and did not return to Ilidza until the end of the war. I only passed through Ilidza." Then just so -- to be fair and to have a full account of this, then at -- two pages later, at 29567, you stated: "... I left Ilidza in 1991. I went to see some friends on occasion in February 1992, and after that I didn't go to Ilidza again." Do you stand by this testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, passing through Ilidza from time to time is not a stay in Ilidza. I understood you to be saying that I passed through Ilidza every now and then during one month or stayed in Ilidza during one month?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just read what you said in your previous case. I'm just asking you: Do you stand by those statements?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were also asked in the Karadzic case, and this is on page 29567: "Q. Did you ever see or hear about paramilitaries in Ilidza, notwithstanding your in-and-out nature?" Your answer was: "I did not see them nor did I hear about them." Do you stand by this testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did not see any paramilitaries there, either Muslim or any other, at Ilidza. But I heard that such Muslim units existed, and I believe that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. So, sir, do I understand correctly you are departing from your previous Karadzic statement that you did not see or hear about paramilitaries in Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: I didn't see them. But as far as I can remember, I did hear about their existence. People asked me where they were being trained and where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's go back to the question that was put to you, Witness. Mr. Weber read to you that in the Karadzic case your testimony was that you did not see them nor that you heard about them. Today you're telling us still that you did not see them but - and that seems to be different - that you did hear about them. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There may have been an error or, rather, maybe I didn't say things through, but I did hear that there were such units at Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you quote from a previous case questions like: "Did you ever see or hear about paramilitaries in Ilidza," of course the Chamber doesn't have any context. So whether it is part of a line of questioning about Serbian paramilitaries or Muslim paramilitaries or both is totally unclear to us. And perhaps for our understanding it would be good --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that also the context is provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honours. I'd be happy to provide it. I see it's the break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's time for a break. Witness, we take a break. And we'd like to see you back, Mr. Dzida, in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so the Chamber has the references for today, the Prosecution has uploaded the Karadzic statement as 65 ter 30709. And the Prosecution has uploaded the Karadzic transcript as 65 ter 30710. It appears I recreated the similar confusion as in the last case, and I will be going to Karadzic transcript page -- strike that. I'll be going to 65 ter 30710, page 18 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- once the witness comes back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Dzida. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, I'm going to read you another part of your Karadzic transcript hopefully to clarify something that we were discussing right before the break. During the Karadzic proceedings, Judge Kwon read you a portion of your statement. He stated: "'During 1990, until 1992, I could not see paramilitary units on Ilidza, which, as it was later found out, the Muslims had already formed in the whole BiH by that time.'" He then asked you: "So here you referred to paramilitary units on Ilidza. Did you mean Serb paramilitary units or Muslim paramilitary units?" You answered: "Your Honours, in this statement I said in 1990 up until 1992, I didn't notice paramilitary units on Ilidza. So it says up to 1992. 1992 isn't taken into account." Judge Kwon, he asked you: "No, my question was whether you meant Muslims or Serbs?" You answered: "Muslims. At the time the Serbs didn't have any units." Do you stand by this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Unless Your Honours have any other questions, I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Throughout portions of your original B/C/S statement in this case, you referred to your brigade as the 1st Rpbr. Could you just please clarify for us what this reference is to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an infantry brigade or, rather, the Romanija Infantry Brigade or, rather, the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 5 of your statement, for the Chamber's reference, you have a sentence that states: "On 20 August 1992, the SRK command sent me to Jabucko Sedlo with the task of pulling out the civilian population and the part of the unit attacked by Muslims." I just want to clarify this location with you. Is Jabucko Sedlo located to the north of Gorazde and the south of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: North of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And located to the south of Rogatica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30702, page 7 of the English and page 6 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, for a little bit here, I'm going to be discussing with you some information -- the information that we have available related to your military service. We do not have much information available for you, so I'm going to be asking you to assist us with explaining a couple of things. Before you is a document from your military records. It is an assessment for the period of 30 June 1991 to 26 September 1996. Can you confirm that this is your signature on the bottom left side of this page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this assessment it indicates that in 1992 and 1993 you were the commander of a CVP company and you were wounded on two occasions. Is this information accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this a military police company?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First it was an infantry company, and then a military police company.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the last portion of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last portion of your answer because the interpreters were unable to catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time I was wounded I was in the infantry company, and then in October 1992 I was reassigned to the military police company. And then the following year on the 6th of May, I was wounded in that company. In the military police company, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The next sentence states: "You were entrusted with the duty of commander of an infantry battalion of the 1st Rpbr." According to your statement in this case, paragraph 5, it indicates that you took up this post on the date of 17 October 1994. Is it correct that the reference in this assessment refers to your assignment as of October 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I was appointed on the 17th of October, 1994, and I became the commander of the 4th Battalion in the Nisici plateau sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the reference in this assessment that -- as to when you were -- that you were commander of an infantry battalion relates to that assignment as of October 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you -- do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might be -- the whole system seems to be ... If I switch on my microphone it doesn't work either. Now it seems to -- could you try again, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this text does not make reference to the time-period when you served as an assistant commander for security and information?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no reference to that. I don't know why that was omitted. I suppose it was a simple mistake, because I discharged those duties as well until the moment when the battalion commander was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your answer's understood. We're going to go through some more information. Do you also agree that this assessment does not specify the brigade which you were part of as a company commander?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman who drafted this, he was a member of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, which was set up after the signing of the Dayton Agreement sometime in February. One brigade arose as a result of that and it was omitted, and there is no reference to any of the documents to the 1st or the 2nd Romanija Brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the English and page 4 of the B/C/S of the same set of materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I did want to go to the first page of this assessment because there is a reference to your post of assistant commander for information and security. On this first page it indicates that you held four posts between the dates of 30 June 1991 and 26 September 1996. Can you see the section where these four posts are indicated?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There's no dates indicated for these, so what I'd like to ask you right now is; what is your best recollection of when you served in the post of assistant commander for information and security?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 9th of August, 1993, up to Easter, which was in April 1994. And then I became the deputy battalion commander after Easter. It was after Easter, I'm sure, but I don't remember the date. On Easter I received the decision for my appointment as the deputy battalion commander, and this assessment was drafted much later, in peacetime, when a new unit had already been set up. That's why there is no reference to all of the units that I served in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You just mentioned a new unit. What unit was that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a peacetime unit which was the 512th Brigade, which was composed of two former brigades. My last appointment was the assistant commander for logistics or, rather, a desk officer for logistics. And I was also the deputy assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30702 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30702 receives number P6544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, I'm now going to go through some additional documents with you and some information is just unclear to us, so we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem at all, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- we'd like you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30705.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a Drina Corps command request number 17/16-25, dated 13 October 1993, to all units. Mr. Dzida, as you can see, the document requests information about those who were killed or wounded from the beginning of the war until May 1992. I have a simple question on this document before we move on to the -- another document. Do you agree that this request is sent to the subordinate units of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say because I don't know. I was in the Sarajevo Corps, and the Drina Corps was set up on the 26th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that there is no reference to this being sent to any units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document could not sent to the SRK if the 2nd Corps sent it to its subordinate units. Only a higher instance could have dispatched it for the 2nd Corps to receive it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, this is what happens if you ask a witness to comment on what apparently is not in a document, then it starts explaining why, and whether that's solid knowledge, yes or no, is a different matter. But if a document does not refer to something, then there is hardly any need to ask a witness whether it does unless that witness has a specific knowledge about the origin of the document or how it was created. But otherwise, what's not in a document, everyone who can read can find out what is not in a document. Again, apart from special circumstances. It's not the first time that you are doing it, so therefore I would encourage you to refrain from these kind of things. If there is any need for the next question for the witness to be aware of it, then you can just put it to the witness that you see nothing is said there, irrespective whether the witness confirms, or agree on the matter with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I do understand and I'll move on. Your Honours, I'm going to be tendering this document, actually, with the next one. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30706.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade response on the same day to the Drina Corps request that we just looked at. I would like to draw your attention to number 4 in the section for "Serious Wounded." It states: "Milorad (Milos) Dzida, from Rogatica, born in," blank, "wounded on 4 May 1992 in Sarajevo, Vrbanja Most." Is it correct that this is a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a reference to me because I was registered with Rogatica municipality, from which the 216th Mountain Brigade came during a mobilisation. From the beginning of the war to its end, I remained with the 1st Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you in the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade on this date, on the 13th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you ever in the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade prior to this date?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never its member save for the time when I went to Jabucko Sedlo to save civilians from Gorazde because they had been encircled by Muslims. That's when I actually arrived in Rogatica municipality. When the Serbs abandoned Gorazde, I returned to my original unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document is from Rajko Kusic. If you need to see it, we can turn to the second page in the B/C/S and the English. Or third page. This document comes from Rajko Kusic. Were you ever under his command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never under his command. I relied on his command for my logistics supply when I was sent to Gorazde to help the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation as to why the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade would be reporting about you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a while ago I told you that the military department in Rogatica is where I was registered. They sent me to serve in the army. I was a military conscript registered with them. Rogatica mobilised people and sent them to the 216th Mountain Brigade. My chart was with that department. I lived in Sarajevo but I never deregistered from the military department in Rogatica; not for military purposes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you could help us clarify that. Is it correct that you were registered as a -- in Rogatica and that is why the records of the Drina Corps reflect that you were possibly one of its members and not the SRK?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a probable explanation. I was never a member of the Rogatica Brigade. I was always in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30705 and 30706 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30705 receives number P6545. And document 30706 receives number P6546, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6545 and P6546 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just like to go through two more documents in a similar fashion, and with the Chamber's instruction, I'll go through the first one rather quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But, sir, I'd like you to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30707.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just going to describe the document to you but I wanted you to see the document. So if after I get done describing it you need anymore time to read it, just please let us know. This is a Drina Corps command request numbered 05/1-377, dated 12 November 1994. So just over a year after the last document we saw. This request asks for updated information on the killed and wounded soldiers. And, sir, if you could look at line number 2 in particular before we go to the next document. It states: "Send the data for the years since the beginning of the war. With regard to 1994, the closing date is 31 October 1994." Sir, I'm just going to ask you, before we go to the next document, have you had enough time to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the Prosecution could now please -- and, Your Honours, just for the record, it appears the witness has nodded that he's looked at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30708.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade response the next day to the Drina Corps request that we just looked at. I'd like to draw your attention to section B before we go on to a later page. Under the section, there is information related to wounded members of the brigade. If you could look at the category row, there are years and then there are the letters T and L underneath the years. Is it correct that the letter T is for the word "tese" or "teze" meaning "seriously wounded," and the letter L is for the word "lakse" meaning "lightly wounded"?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be so. T, seriously, and L, lightly wounded. But once again, it's a document from the Drina Corps and not from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to go through some information on this before we go to the next page. Under Roman numeral --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, how do we have to understand the footnotes in relation to letters T and L in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do not think that they are accurate. I leave it in the context of the document. That's why I was asking the witness to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, they do not appear in the original and therefore you suggest that we ignore those comments contained in those footnotes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under Roman numeral II, there is data for reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could follow me across on the row for officers, this row indicates that there were two reserve officers who were seriously wounded and six reserve officers who were lightly wounded in 1992. One reserve officer who was seriously wounded in 1993. And then if you go across the row, the total appears to bring it to three seriously wounded officers and six lightly wounded reserve officers. Do you see the row that I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 4 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there is a list attached to this response. Under the heavily wounded section, there are three officers listed: Two in 1992 and one in 1993. Under the section for lightly wounded officers, there are six individuals listed, all from 1992, and it appears your name is listed at number two. Would your explanation of this document be the same as what you previously stated with respect to the documents we looked at from 1993, your explanation for being included as part of the Drina Corps records?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you how it could be possible that the military department provided the information to the Rogatica Brigade, as I don't see how else it could have been. I was never subordinated to the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 30707 and 30708 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you may after I have heard the numbers from Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Documents 30707 receives number P6547, and document 30708 receives number P6548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This time, the first time when I was wounded, I was a member of the Yugoslav People's Army because the Army of Republika Srpska had not yet been established and the reports were sent to military departments. That's most probably why I figure in this list. Because I was wounded the first time on the 6th of May -- excuse me, the 4th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P6547 and P6548 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move on to a new topic now and discuss your statements in first the Karadzic case and then the Mladic case. Is it correct that you provided a statement in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to signing that statement, is it correct that you were interviewed on at least two occasions by members of the Karadzic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The names of the individuals who interviewed you from the Karadzic Defence team were Slobodan Batnic [phoen] and Milomir Savcic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You knew both of these individuals prior to your interviews with them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Superficially.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that you knew them from during the war?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a little, superficially. I may have met them in passing and so on. We didn't have anything in common.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you knew them from during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard of them but we didn't socialise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you knew them from during the war. That is a time-period. Not where, not what you were wearing, not what you spoke about, but whether it was during the war that you got to know them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't meet during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then tell us when you -- since when you knew them and how you knew them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With Milomir I had coffee for the first time when we conducted the interview here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D489.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you will be your statement in this case, the Mladic case. Is it correct that you were interviewed on four occasions prior to your signing this statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately how long each of these interviews were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They lasted at least an hour to an hour and a half each. I usually had to leave and I was in a rush because I had some obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you know Mr. Slavko Gengo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. He used to be my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In Mr. Gengo's statement that is admitted in this case, it indicates that he was interviewed on two of the same dates as you; these dates being the 28th and 29th of October, 2013. Did you see Mr. Gengo on either of these dates?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I just don't remember which dates they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was -- when you saw Mr. Gengo on either the 28th or 29th of October, 2013, was anyone else present besides the two of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were never together. We were always separate. I always insisted to finish as soon as possible. I had to complete my work because I had to perform some work at a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. According to the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could please go to the last page, which I believe contains the date that it was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this statement, it indicates that you signed this on the 10th of May, 2014. This also corresponds to the date Mr. Gengo signed his statement. Did you see him on that date, 10 May 2014?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was the most recent occasion that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask -- perhaps, Mr. Weber, could I ask, then, a few questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The 10th of May, where did you sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you be a bit more precise, where in Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a building called the Tradesmen's Centre in Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you made some corrections to your statement. Recently we received the corrections. Apparently they were made in The Hague although there is no date on it. This signed correction, did you sign that when you -- after your arrival in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the 10th of May, why did you not make the corrections on that day? Could you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 10th of May I read it and I didn't immediately notice that there were any typos or errors. And then later on, I corrected them at home, when I read the statement for the second or third time. It was then that I corrected the errors. And so some of my recollections were left out. They were not recorded. And I had forgotten or I didn't have enough time when I was with President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you didn't have enough time when you were with -- let me read it again. With President Karadzic. Could you explain that. When did you have not sufficient time for what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, when the public prosecutor lady asked me, I couldn't remember the name because she kept interrupting me, and I had no time, the time that was allowed to me to answer some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I'm talking about your statement, the statement as we received it. Or is that a statement which is the same as the statement you gave in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you read it on the 10th of May. How much time did you have to read it on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as I remember, up to 25 or 30 minutes, because I needed about five to six minutes per page to read it and sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was the most recent occasion that you have seen or spoken with Slavko Gengo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before my departure I saw him passing and I talked to him from a car. And I saw him when I arrived here as well, and then we talked but not about the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw him before your departure, where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pale. As far as I remember, I think it was near the Dva Goluba cafe restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you arrive in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you see Slavko Gengo after the 16th of May?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in Belgrade at the airport, and I was surprised because I didn't know at the time that he was travelling too. But he was accommodated in a different hotel, and two or three days later we happened to meet accidentally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: To understand correctly, is it correct that the two of you travelled here to The Hague together on the 16th of May?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know, was he the only other witness in this case with whom you travelled together or were there more persons on that same plane that travelled to The Hague in order to appear as witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Because we didn't sit together. I sat far away from him, so we were not close to each other on the plane, and I didn't know anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You said you saw him two or three days after your arrival. Did you speak with him at any other time after your arrival in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that we talked but we never discussed the cases because of which we came here. When we were received by the VWS, we got a paper telling us that it was prohibited to discuss such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you watch Mr. Gengo's testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since you've been in The Hague, have you seen any other witnesses who have appeared or will appear during these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a few. But I hadn't known most of them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to go back to one more simple question. Is -- could you tell us approximately how many times per year you see Slavko Gengo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few. If you want the numbers, perhaps four or five times. But we would meet briefly. I am retired and I sometimes work on the basis of contracts and I work for 10 or 12 hours a day, so I just go to work or I'm at home. When I have free time, I go to my native village and there I till some land, so I have very little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to move on to actually another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- may I put a question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am referring to the beginning of page 42 of today's transcript. Sir, you were asked by Mr. Weber about the 28th and 29th of October, 2013, when you were interviewed by the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. And Mr. Weber asked you: "Did you see Mr. Gengo on either of these days?" And your answer was: "I did. I just don't remember which dates they were." Then the next question of Mr. Weber was more or less: Was anyone else present besides the two of you? And then your answer was: "We were never together. We were always separate." Can you explain that, that you saw Mr. Gengo, yes, and that you were never together? I would like to understand the situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him in passing here, but we were not together in the same office when we had to do this with regard to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are saying that you saw him here. Was that interview conducted here in The Hague or in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the corridor, in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which corridor? Here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The corridor of the rooms where we met with the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm asking you about end of October 2013. Was that -- did that happen here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were not together in the same room even then, not together at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Here in The Hague or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 29th of October, I'm talking about this date, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where? Here in The Hague or where else?
